judged_text: Attendee rows are committed at the prisma.booking.update before the calendar update and email send run, with no compensation, and the duplicate filter subsequently treats those persisted guests as already-existing attendees. When updateCalendarAttendees throws (e.g. an expired calendar token), the mutation returns an error with the guests already stored but never emailed or calendar-added, and the user's retry is rejected with BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid — the operation can never be completed.

record.issue_text: [BUG] Attendee rows are committed at the prisma.booking.update before the calendar update and email send run, with no compensation, and the duplicate filter subsequently treats those persisted guests as already-existing attendees. When updateCalendarAttendees throws (e.g. an expired calendar token), the mutation returns an error with the guests already stored but never emailed or calendar-added, and the user's retry is rejected with BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid — the operation can never be completed.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` before calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and before sending emails. There is no transaction/rollback/compensation. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the handler will error out (not caught), leaving guests stored in DB but without calendar sync and without emails. On retry, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails already present in `booking.attendees`, which will now include the previously-persisted guests, making `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and causing `BAD_REQUEST` (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`). This matches the finding: a partial write makes the operation non-retriable and permanently incomplete.
